values.value: 32 record slots of one 256-byte page each, in the last 2 sectors of 4,096 bytes of the 2 MB
values.source: firmware/iomcu/src/out_store.c:30-39; Research.md:102; read 2026-09-28 from the checkout at be1f247
values.refutation_tried: STORE_RECORDS is 4,096 / 256 = 16 a sector, so 2 sectors give 32 slots. The code places them at 4 MB less 8 kB (out_store.c:35-39) for the module build; 2 MB less 8 kB is the change Research.md:102 requires. Today's record is 148 bytes: a 20-byte header plus 32 and 32 uint16 registers for 8 slots and 8 channels (out_store.c:99-107; LINK_OS_COUNT and LINK_CC_COUNT in link_pages.h). The record for the IO board's 20 ports is not defined (IOBoard.md:248), so its size is not known (question 15).

questions.question: Which motor temperature channel, infrared or thermocouple, fills the BENCH page's one motor temperature register (register 5, 0.1 °C signed, valid bit 4)? Or does a second register carry the other channel?
questions.why: The BENCH page has one motor temperature register and one valid bit (shared/link/include/link_pages.h:235, :269), and F5 fixes 2 channels (IOBoard.md:458, :483). Without the answer P2 cannot state which channel's reading the register's 0.1 °C signed format and the 20 ms bench sampling apply to. Nor can it state whether the other channel feeds a register that does not exist yet.

questions.question: Which thermocouple type (a letter, such as K, J or T) does the thermocouple channel take?
questions.why: F5 names a thermocouple and no type (Research.md:533). P2 checks each front end's supported types and linearisation, and the type sets the range question 2 applies.

questions.question: What motor temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) must the thermocouple channel measure?
questions.why: Neither page states a range. The register's -3,276.8 to +3,276.7 °C span (link_pages.h:234-235) bounds nothing. P2 checks each front end's measurement range for the type against it.

questions.question: What accuracy (± °C) must the thermocouple channel give over that range, cold-junction compensation included?
questions.why: Neither page states an accuracy. The register's 0.1 °C step (IOBoard.md:459) is the link's step, not an accuracy. P2 compares each front end's datasheet error, conversion and cold junction together, against it. The cold junction sits at the IO board's connector (IOBoard.md:558). The only ambient range the pages state is the monostable's, 0 to 50 °C (hardware/docs/Monostable.md:27 at 23c82ca).

questions.question: How often (Hz) must the thermocouple channel deliver a new reading?
questions.why: The coprocessor samples the bench numbers every 20 ms (IOBoard.md:431). That is the firmware loop, not a stated need for motor temperature. P2 checks each front end's conversion time, with its filter setting, against it.

questions.question: What voltage (V) must the thermocouple input withstand, without damage, between either lead and the IO board's ground if the junction touches a motor phase or winding?
questions.why: The motor runs from the ESC pack of up to 67.2 V (F15, Research.md:543), and the phase-wire clip is rated for it (IOBoard.md:443). The thermocouple input carries no rating on either page. P2 checks each front end's input absolute maximum or protection against it, or qualifies an isolated input.

questions.question: How long (m) is the lead from the IO board's infrared connector to the infrared sensor at the motor? Answer 0 m if the sensor sits on the IO board.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:558 gives the infrared channel a connector, so the sensor sits off the board. The length decides whether the sensor is a part off the board, bought at Digi-Key with LCSC number none (sourcing rule 1, Research.md:134-139). It also decides which interface the lead carries: a digital sensor's bus capacitance or an analogue signal.

questions.question: What object temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) must the infrared channel measure?
questions.why: F5 gives an infrared channel and no range (Research.md:533). P2 checks each sensor's object temperature range against it.

questions.question: What accuracy (± °C) must the infrared channel give over that range?
questions.why: Neither page states an accuracy. P2 compares each sensor's datasheet object-temperature accuracy over the range of question 7 against it.

questions.question: What full field of view (degrees) must the infrared sensor have, given its distance to the motor and the surface it must see?
questions.why: An infrared thermometer averages everything inside its field of view, so a view wider than the motor at the mounting distance reads the surroundings. Neither page gives the distance or the surface. P2 selects the sensor's optics variant against it.

questions.question: How often (Hz) must the infrared channel deliver a new reading?
questions.why: The 20 ms bench sampling (IOBoard.md:431) is the firmware loop, not a stated need. P2 checks each sensor's refresh rate against it.

questions.question: At which clock rate (kHz) must the external I2C ports run?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:481 records the coprocessor's I2C bus speed as not stated. The one I2C speed setting, 100 to 400 kHz, belongs to the display's bus (shared/settings/settings.c:105-107, IOBoard.md:597). P2 checks each multiplexer, buffer or extender's rated clock against it (seeds TCA9548A, PCA9615, TCA9617A). The infrared sensor and the store share the coprocessor's buses.

questions.question: What is the longest cable (m) between an external I2C port and the device on it?
questions.why: Q7 fixes 2 Qwiic ports at 3.3 V but no cable length or bus capacitance (Research.md:545). The length decides whether a port needs a buffer or a differential extender, and the capacitance each part must drive.

questions.question: What current (mA) must each external I2C port supply on its 3.3 V pin?
questions.why: A Qwiic port carries its device's 3.3 V supply, and neither page states the current. P2 needs it for a port switch or current limit. R5 sizes the 3.3 V rail from the parts the tasks select, which leaves external devices out (Research.md:283).

questions.question: Which 7-bit I2C addresses (hex) must a device on an external I2C port be free to use?
questions.why: The original requirement puts external current sensors on these ports (docs/Manifest.md:14, :28). The port monitors hold 0x40 to 0x43, and each INA238 0x44 or above, on the RP2354B's 2 I2C buses (IOBoard.md:351, :464). The answer decides whether a port may share a bus with them or needs its own segment behind a multiplexer.

questions.question: What capacity (bytes) must an I2C FRAM or EEPROM store hold for the IO board's output binding?
questions.why: The flash store holds 32 slots of 256 bytes, 8,192 bytes (IOBoard.md:115). Today's record is 148 bytes for 8 slots and 8 channels (firmware/iomcu/src/out_store.c:99-107). The IO board's 20-port record is not defined (IOBoard.md:248). By their part numbers the seeds run from 16 Kbit (FM24CL16B) to 256 Kbit (MB85RC256V, 24LC256). P2 checks each FRAM or EEPROM candidate's capacity against it.

questions.question: How many saves (count) of the output binding must the store survive over the board's life?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:117 gives what the flash store allows: about 3.2 million saves, at 100,000 cycles a sector over 32 slots. Neither page states how many saves the board needs. P2 checks each FRAM or EEPROM candidate's write endurance against it.
